title: Lag Between the New Coverage's Effective Date and the Coverage-Inactive Denial — Home Oxygen Therapy
content:
# Lag of the Coverage-Inactive Denial After the Effective Date — Home Oxygen Therapy

**Rule.** When a different coverage becomes primary for Home Oxygen Therapy, the first day of service found from the claim history replaces the effective date only when the most recent coverage-inactive denial from the earlier coverage was adjudicated no more than the lag below after the new coverage's effective date. The earlier coverage is the coverage the oxygen record names; its class is read from the patient's Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility records. Days are calendar days, counted as the later date less the earlier date. When the earlier coverage has no coverage-inactive denial on the oxygen claim history, the denial lag is met. When the condition fails, the first day of service is the effective date.

| Class of the earlier coverage | Lag (days after the new coverage's effective date) |
|---|---|
| Commercial PPO, Commercial HMO | 60 |
| Medicare Advantage PPO, Medicare Advantage HMO | 45 |
| any other class (for example Original Medicare Part B, Medicaid Fee-for-Service) | 30 |

## Both sides (hypothetical, effective date 1 March)

| Earlier coverage class | Denial adjudicated | Days after 1 March | Condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Commercial HMO | 30 April | 60 | met |
| Commercial HMO | 1 May | 61 | fails |
| Medicare Advantage PPO | 15 April | 45 | met |
| Medicare Advantage PPO | 16 April | 46 | fails |
| Original Medicare Part B | 31 March | 30 | met |
| Original Medicare Part B | 1 April | 31 | fails |
| any class | no coverage-inactive denial on the claim history | — | met |
